title.analysis: Authentic title "Retire on $1,000,000? The Shocking Reality" frames a negative surprise. The script concludes a million plus Social Security supports a middle-class retirement ("not yacht money, but not cat food money"), so "shocking" overstates. The question form matches the content.

script.opening_words: Picture this. Uh, you finally hit the magical $1 million mark in your retirement savings. You're probably thinking you've made it, right? Uh, time to buy that yacht, upgrade to first class forever, and maybe even consider hiring someone to tie your shoes for you. Well, hold on to your wallet because what I'm about to tell you might just burst that bubble faster than a cheap pool float at a family barbecue. The harsh reality is that $1 million
script.ending_words: assuming you add social security into the mix. It's not exactly yacht money, but it's not cat food money either. The key is managing your expectations and planning accordingly. Because retirement surprises are about as welcome as finding out your dentist has expensive hobbies. Start planning now. Stay realistic about what your money can actually do. And remember that a comfortable retirement is still absolutely achievable with the right strategy.
script.analysis: Full 19800 canonical characters read. A single-narrator, joke-heavy explainer: hook on hitting $1M, market volatility and 2018, inflation, 3%/4%/5% withdrawal rates, 4% rule assumptions, longevity, Social Security top-up, account taxes, state taxes and geography, health care, replacement ratio, retirement age, alternative income, sequence risk and cash buffer, taxable-account events, a practical $60K budget, IRMAA and long-term care, and a summary. Arithmetic reproduces; the Social Security average is stale, two passages are scrambled, and the summary range contradicts the body.
